**Andrew Fetterly Wilkes-Krier** (born May 9, 1979), known professionally as **Andrew W.K.**, is an American singer, multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, record producer and motivational speaker. He is known for his combination of [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") music and anthemic songs about partying.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-4)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) Raised in Michigan, Wilkes-Krier began his musical career in the mid-1990s. He performed in a number of local bands before eventually moving to New York, where he produced his first recordings under the Andrew W.K. moniker.

After gaining initial attention with the 2000 [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play")_Girls Own Juice_, Wilkes-Krier rose to prominence with the release of his debut studio album _[I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Get\_Wet "I Get Wet")_ in November 2001, which was followed by _[The Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")_ (2003) and _[Close Calls With Brick Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close\_Calls\_With\_Brick\_Walls "Close Calls With Brick Walls")_ (2006). Legal troubles preventing Wilkes-Krier from releasing music in the US led up to him making the album _[55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55\_Cadillac "55 Cadillac")_ (2009), which consists of solo [improvisational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_improvisation "Musical improvisation") piano pieces.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Goodman-5) He returned to rock music with the albums _[You're Not Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Not\_Alone\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")_ (2018) and _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_ (2021). The instrumental [jazz-noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_jazz "Crime jazz") album _[Temptation to Exist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temptation\_to\_Exist?action=edit&redlink=1 "Temptation to Exist (page does not exist)")_ (2026) was [surprise released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") after a five-year hiatus.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-6) He has also undertaken a number of other musical and non-musical ventures including television and radio work, motivational speaking and writing.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Andrew Fetterly Wilkes-Krier[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-7) was born in [Stanford, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford,_California "Stanford, California"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) on May 9, 1979[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-livewire-9) and raised in the outskirts of [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), until moving to [Ann Arbor, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Arbor,_Michigan "Ann Arbor, Michigan") at the age of four.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-livewire-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-10) His father is professor [James E. Krier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Krier "James E. Krier"), a legal scholar at the [University of Michigan Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School "University of Michigan Law School") and co-author of the widely used Dukeminier & Krier property casebook.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11) His mother is Wendy Wilkes. His younger brother, Patrick, was a golf professional and is now a golf coach in Michigan.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-12) At the age of four, Wilkes-Krier began learning piano at the [University of Michigan School of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_School_of_Music,_Theatre_&_Dance "University of Michigan School of Music, Theatre & Dance").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Enders-13) He has recalled early family trips to [midnight mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_mass "Midnight mass") as having had an enormous impact on his love for music.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-14)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He was dubbed Andrew W.K. by an elementary school teacher to differentiate him from his classmates [Andrew Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Hawthorne "Mayer Hawthorne") and Andrew Gilchrist.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He later attended the private college preparatory [Greenhills School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhills_School "Greenhills School") for middle school before attending the alternative [Community High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_High_School_(Ann_Arbor,_Michigan) "Community High School (Ann Arbor, Michigan)") from 1993 to 1997, where he continued to study piano and keyboard.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Enders-13)

## Music career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music career")]

### 1993–1999: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1993–1999: Early career")]

In 1993, at the age of 14, he joined the band Slam, later to be called Reverse Polarity.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) In 1996, a song recorded by W.K. entitled "Mr. Surprise" was included on _Plant the Flower Seeds_, a compilation by the [Ypsilanti, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ypsilanti,_Michigan "Ypsilanti, Michigan")-based record label Westside Audio Laboratories, marking his first publicly released recording.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201418-17) Over the next five years, W.K. would play in a number of Detroit-based [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") bands,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) including The Pterodactyls; Lab Lobotomy; Music Band; Mr. Velocity Hopkins; playing drums in [grindcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grindcore "Grindcore") metal band, Kathode;[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) in addition to forming the [noise rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_rock "Noise rock") project Ancient Art of Boar, later known as AAB, which served as an outlet for his early solo material.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)

In 1998, W.K. moved from Michigan to New York City, where he worked a variety of short-lived jobs. These included a bubblegum machine salesman, an opera ticket salesman, a fashion photographer, a window decorator at the [Bergdorf Goodman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergdorf_Goodman "Bergdorf Goodman") department store, and a waiter for a Mexican restaurant. He also worked at the offices of the avant-garde fashion company [Comme des Garçons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comme_des_Gar%C3%A7ons "Comme des Garçons").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He ended the AAB project and began recording new solo material under his full "Andrew Wilkes-Krier" name; the year saw the release of a cassette-only single entitled _Room to Breathe_ on [Hanson Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanson_Records "Hanson Records").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) A follow-up release entitled _You Are What You Eat_ was scrapped when the master recordings went missing.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-18) W.K. also recorded the soundtrack for an independent film named _Poltergeist_ made by [Aaron Dilloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Dilloway "Aaron Dilloway") and himself, one track of which appeared on the Hanson Records compilation _Labyrinths & Jokes_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) In 1999, he moved to [Seffner, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seffner,_Florida "Seffner, Florida"), to start building his live band with drummer [Donald "D.T." Tardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Tardy "Donald Tardy"), of [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal") band [Obituary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obituary_(band) "Obituary (band)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)

### 2000–2003: Solo breakthrough, _I Get Wet_ and _The Wolf_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2000–2003: Solo breakthrough, I Get Wet and The Wolf")]

Main articles: [I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Get_Wet "I Get Wet") and [The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wolf_(Andrew_W.K._album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")

In March 2000, Wilkes-Krier released his first [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), _Girls Own Juice_, also abbreviated as _AWKGOJ_, on [Bulb Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulb_Records "Bulb Records"), his first solo release under the moniker Andrew W.K. (He had first been credited as "Andrew W.K." on a remix entitled "Wolf Eyes Rules (What Kinda Band?)" for the experimental noise band [Wolf Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf_Eyes "Wolf Eyes").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201452-19)) _Girls Own Juice_ introduced his [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock")-influenced musical style and experimental tendencies, described as "[Judas Priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judas_Priest "Judas Priest") mixed with [Sparks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparks_(band) "Sparks (band)")" by Magas, a collaborator of W.K.'s.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201453-20)

_Girls Own Juice_ was well received by critics, and was awarded a five-star rating by the British music magazine _[Kerrang!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerrang! "Kerrang!")._[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-21) The release increased buzz for W.K., centered around his "hedonistic, so-dumb-it's-smart rawk."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) He continued to build his reputation by performing various solo gigs in the New York and other East Coast areas. Wilkes-Krier and his then manager [Matt Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Sweeney "Matt Sweeney") later shipped out a number of Andrew W.K. demo tapes, each accompanied by a handwritten letter. One tape reached [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock") musician [Dave Grohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Grohl "Dave Grohl"); impressed, Grohl offered Andrew W.K. a slot opening for his band [Foo Fighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_Fighters "Foo Fighters") at a concert in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), which he accepted.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22)

Another tape reached [The Island Def Jam Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Island_Def_Jam_Music_Group "The Island Def Jam Music Group") executive Lewis Largent, who liked the demos enough to attend an Andrew W.K. gig at the [Mercury Lounge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Lounge "Mercury Lounge"), where Largent was impressed by how W.K. "won over every last person in the audience."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22) Wilkes-Krier reacted with surprise to Island's interest in him, and despite his manager urging him not to accept his very first offer, W.K. was eager to begin work with Island.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22)_Girls Own Juice_ was followed by another Bulb Records EP entitled _[Party Til You Puke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party\_Til\_You\_Puke "Party Til You Puke")_ in October 2000.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) Following the release of _Party Til You Puke_, Andrew W.K. left Bulb Records amicably to sign with [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)

W.K.'s major-label debut studio album, _[I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Get\_Wet "I Get Wet")_, was released on November 13, 2001, on Island Records.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Klosterman-24) Continuing the sound established by his previous Bulb Records EPs, _I Get Wet_ is characterized by its [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") and [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") influences and lyrical content revolving around partying.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) The album is known for its cover art, a photograph by [Roe Ethridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roe_Ethridge "Roe Ethridge") of Andrew W.K. with a stream of blood running from his nose onto his chin and neck,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-25) which generated minor controversy in Europe after it was seen to represent [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine") abuse;[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-26) W.K. claims to have achieved the effect by striking himself in the face with a cinderblock during the photo shoot, and subsequently supplementing his own blood with some of an animal obtained from a butcher's shop.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8)

_I Get Wet_ earned positive press from publications such as _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ and _[Kerrang!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerrang! "Kerrang!")_ and featured two UK hit singles, "[Party Hard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Hard_(Andrew_W.K._song) "Party Hard (Andrew W.K. song)")" and "[She Is Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Is_Beautiful "She Is Beautiful")", also rising to the top spot on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Top Heatseekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Heatseekers "Top Heatseekers") albums chart.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-27) She Is Beautiful was also featured on the 2003 [_Freaky Friday_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky_Friday_(soundtrack) "Freaky Friday (soundtrack)"). At the same time, W.K. also developed a reputation for his highly energetic live shows.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) Andrew W.K. joined [Ozzy Osbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzy_Osbourne "Ozzy Osbourne")'s [Ozzfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzfest "Ozzfest") that summer, and a number of _I Get Wet_'s tracks, such as "Party Hard", "It's Time to Party", and "Fun Night" were licensed for use in various video games, films, TV series, and commercials. In 2002, W.K., Gibson Goodness and Alec Rominger re-recorded his song "We Want Fun" from _AWKGOJ_ for the soundtrack of _[Jackass: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackass:\_The\_Movie "Jackass: The Movie")_; an accompanying music video was also produced, filmed and directed by [Jeff Tremaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Tremaine "Jeff Tremaine") with additional camera work by [Spike Jonze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Jonze "Spike Jonze"). By September 2018, the album had sold 267,000 copies in the US.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-28)

In late 2003, W.K. released his second studio album _[The Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")_. In contrast to _I Get Wet_, which was recorded by W.K. with his live band, _The Wolf_ featured W.K. playing all instruments, with heavy use of [overdubbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overdub "Overdub") of these instrument sections in production. The album spawned the singles "Tear It Up" and "Never Let Down" in the United States, while the song "Long Live the Party" was a minor hit in Japan. The single "Tear It Up" was included as menu music in the video-game Nascar Thunder TM 2004.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11) Despite earning Andrew W.K.'s highest chart position ever at #61 on the Billboard 200, it fell off after only a week,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-29) and three months after its release the album had only sold 36,098 copies.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-30)

On tour for _The Wolf_, W.K. was injured on stage and broke his foot. After the concert, he signed autographs from the ambulance. Not wanting to let his fans down, he performed the remainder of the tour in a wheelchair.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8)

### 2009–2019: _55 Cadillac_, _You're Not Alone_ and other releases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2009–2019: 55 Cadillac, You're Not Alone and other releases")]

Main articles: [55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55_Cadillac "55 Cadillac") and [You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're_Not_Alone_(Andrew_W.K._album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")

In February 2009, Wilkes-Krier claimed to have found a loophole in his contractual constraints allowing him to form his own record label, Skyscraper Music Maker, based in London and Manhattan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-label-32) The label released _DAMN! The Mix tape Vol. 1_ on May 25, 2009, a compilation of W.K.'s production work for Skyscraper Music Maker artists Bad Brilliance, Aleister X, and [Cherie Lily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherie_Lily "Cherie Lily"), with music by New York producer, DJ B-Roc.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-label-32) Wilkes-Krier's fifth studio album _[55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55\_Cadillac "55 Cadillac")_ served as the label's second release. Recorded entirely by Wilkes-Krier and consisting of his spontaneous solo piano improvisations, the album was released on September 8, 2009.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-33) In a piece written to accompany the release of the album, he explained that the last decade had "been so fraught with legal trouble" that he began to suffer hallucinations, which inspired him to produce the album, and that successful negotiations had allowed him to start a new label and release _55 Cadillac_, which he described as "the sound of a piano being played by a free man – nothing more, nothing less."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-33) New negotiations were undertaken over the UK release of _55 Cadillac_, as "certain people [who] weren't credited because they weren't involved with the recording... had to be given credit," owing to previous contracts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) Wilkes-Krier and his management settled by renaming Skyscraper Music Maker as Steev Mike, which the parties involved saw as a reasonable compromise.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) All prior complaints were dropped and Wilkes-Krier was then allowed to release the album worldwide.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34)

On September 9, Andrew W.K. released a Japan-only album entitled _[Gundam Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gundam\_Rock "Gundam Rock")_, consisting of covered music from the [Gundam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gundam "Gundam") anime television series to celebrate its 30th anniversary in Japan; he had been approached by Japanese animation studio [Sunrise Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrise_(company) "Sunrise (company)") to record the album following the success of _The Japan Covers_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-37) With all prior legal disputes over credit and naming settled, in March 2010 Andrew W.K. and the newly named Steev Mike label presented its first official release: a repackaged two-disc version of _Close Calls with Brick Walls_ with a bonus disc of rare and unreleased material entitled _Mother of Mankind_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) To promote the set, Andrew W.K. joined the 2010 [Warped Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warped_Tour "Warped Tour") as a headlining act for the entire tour.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Warped_Tour_2010-38) A music video for the single "I Want to See You Go Wild" from _Close Calls with Brick Walls_, directed by [Peter Glantz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Glantz "Peter Glantz"), was released in June 2010.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-39)

In March 2011, Andrew W.K. released a new EP entitled _[The "Party All Goddamn Night" EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_%22Party\_All\_Goddamn\_Night%22\_EP "The \"Party All Goddamn Night\" EP")_, which consists of five new tracks and two previously released singles.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-40) In September 2012, while attending a fan convention for _[My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Little\_Pony:\_Friendship\_Is\_Magic "My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic")_, he expressed the possibility of recording a new album.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-41) In a [Reddit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reddit "Reddit") "Ask Me Anything" thread in October 2014, Wilkes-Krier stated that while his other career ventures had kept him from releasing a new studio album, he was eager to record one: "I've been stock-piling new songs for several years. I really want to make a new album as soon as possible."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-42)

In September 2017, W.K. announced that a new studio album would be set for release on March 2, 2018, via [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-43) In November, he announced its title, _[You're Not Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Not\_Alone\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")_, and shared its cover artwork.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-45) The album was released on March 2, 2018. In August 2018 he revealed to _Riff Magazine_ that he had begun recording his next album.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-46)

### 2020–present: Napalm Records, _God Is Partying_, _Temptation To Exist_ and current ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020–present: Napalm Records, God Is Partying, Temptation To Exist and current ventures")]

Main article: [God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Is_Partying "God Is Partying")

In October 2020, Andrew W.K. signed with [Napalm Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napalm_Records "Napalm Records") and announced that he was working on a new album.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-47) The lead single "Babalon" was released on February 17, 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-48) "Babalon" was announced via a Napalm Records press release and made available for limited pre-order on the Napalm Records and Andrew W.K. stores as a 7" vinyl with the instrumental B-Side "The Party Gods".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-:0-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-50) The release, limited to 393 copies, marked a departure from Andrew W.K.'s traditionally positive and uplifting themes, and features "swinging drums and a sinister guitar riff opening the track's hellish gates."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-:0-49)

Andrew W.K.'s sixth studio album, _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_, was released on September 10, 2021.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-51) Co-produced by long-time recording partner Ted Young, the nine-track album features W.K. performing all instruments.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-52) The announcement was accompanied by the release of a new single, "I'm in Heaven".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-53) On July 14, 2021, the video for "Everybody Sins" was released and features an appearance by [Kat Dennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kat_Dennings "Kat Dennings").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-54) In September 2021, the album _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_ was released alongside the single "Stay True To Your Heart".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-56)

Shortly after the release of the album, W.K. delayed upcoming shows and deleted his website and social media pages with no explanation; his label also remained quiet on what was happening.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-58)

On August 28, 2026, W.K. released the album _Temptation to Exist_ on the fan run website AWKSHARE and through YouTube Music. [[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-59)

## Other ventures

### Self-help and motivational performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Self-help and motivational performance")]

During 2007, Andrew performed a series of unpredictable [happenings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happening "Happening") as part of his "One Man Show" tour. Each event began with Andrew improvising on the piano alone on a stage before they frequently evolved into giant parties, with most of the audience dancing on stage with Andrew, themselves playing the piano and singing the lyrics.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)

In March 2007, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ put Andrew on the front page of its Arts section, in a feature article on Andrew's lectures.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-60) In 2008, Andrew's self-help work led to his second appearance as a sit-down guest on _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-61) In November 2008, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine called him "truly cute".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)

In June 2012, W.K. announced that he would be appearing at the _[My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Little\_Pony:\_Friendship\_Is\_Magic "My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic")_ fan convention Canterlot Gardens.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-62) His appearance was announced as a motivational seminar on "How to Party like Pinkie Pie", based on one of the show's lead characters, Pinkie Pie. The appearance was featured in _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-rollingstone.com-63) and was co-hosted by musician and personality Klisk Midori.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Klisk-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-rollingstone.com2-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-everfree.net-66)

In June 2014, Andrew was announced to speak as a guest lecturer at the [Oxford Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_Union "Oxford Union").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-67) W.K.'s keynote, titled _Andrew W.K. and The Philosophy of Partying_, discussed his signature message of positive power and celebratory self-confidence. Regarding the lecture, Oxford's Nick Fowler said: "In my opinion, Andrew is one of Rock N' Roll's great philosophers." And the Oxford University Rock Society offered their own statement: "We've seen rock stars, we've seen brilliant public speakers, but rarely are they the same person, and rarely do they have as intriguing and broad a background as Andrew W.K."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-68)

In September 2014, Andrew gave a lecture on his philosophy of partying at [Baltimore School for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_School_for_the_Arts "Baltimore School for the Arts") as part of The Contemporary museum's speaker series called "CoHosts".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-69) In the same month, he also brought his Village Voice advice column, "Ask Andrew W.K.", to life in an intimate setting at New York City nightclub, [Santos Party House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Party_House "Santos Party House").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-70)

In February 2018, Andrew was named the Person of the Year by the [American Association of Suicidology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Suicidology "American Association of Suicidology").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-71) The AAS stated, "The inaugural Person of the Year Award will be presented to Andrew W.K. due to his consistent and powerful use of positivity to improve the lives of those who hear his music."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-72)

### Production work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Production work")]

In addition to producing his own music on the albums _I Get Wet_, _The Wolf_, _Close Calls with Brick Walls_, and _You're Not Alone_, Andrew has produced and mixed music for other artists as well as working on special commercial music projects. These include the production of music exclusively for commercial use on television and radio.

In 2008, Andrew gained new notoriety for recording a song called "The McLaughlin Groove", based on an exchange between [Pat Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Buchanan "Pat Buchanan") and [John McLaughlin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_McLaughlin_(host) "John McLaughlin (host)") on the political television show _[The McLaughlin Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_McLaughlin\_Group "The McLaughlin Group")_. The song was commissioned by the Public Radio International show _Fair Game_, on which Andrew has appeared for interviews.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-95)

In 2004, Andrew recorded a television jingle for [Kit Kat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kit_Kat "Kit Kat") candy bars, and rewrote their trademark "Give Me a Break" slogan into a new song.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) The recording appeared in a variety of 30-second, 45-second, and 1 minute commercials, broadcast on television worldwide. "I avoided working with other people for many years, partly out of paranoia, and partly out of an earnest desire to stand on my own. After a while, I got tired of thinking that way, and it just seemed natural to do the opposite of what I had done before. I like making music with other people. I can still make music by myself too."[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-96)

Andrew's earliest external production work was with the group [Wolf Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf_Eyes "Wolf Eyes"), on their now out-of-print 12-inch EP _Fortune Dove_. The last track on that album, "What Kind of Band?" features Andrew W.K. on vocals explaining why he enjoys listening to Wolf Eyes. Since then, he's chosen to work on a select and seemingly random set of projects, beginning with production and mixing on the album, _Through The Panama_, by Brooklyn, NY based three-piece [art rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_rock "Art rock") band, [Sightings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sightings_(band) "Sightings (band)"). The album was jointly released by Load Records and [Thurston Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thurston_Moore "Thurston Moore")'s [Ecstatic Peace!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecstatic_Peace! "Ecstatic Peace!") label in October 2007.

At the end of 2007, Andrew accepted an invitation to produce a new album, _Repentance_, for veteran reggae artist [Lee "Scratch" Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_%22Scratch%22_Perry "Lee \"Scratch\" Perry"). The two had met when Andrew interviewed Perry for DirecTV.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-97)_Repentance_ was nominated for "Best Reggae Album" in the 2009 Grammy Awards.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-98) On February 20, 2008, Andrew released an exclusive ringtone commissioned by Universal Music Japan for the Japanese mobile phone market. The song is called, "Sonna no Kankei Ne Rock", which celebrates a then popular catch-phrase by a TV Talent, "Sonna no Kankei Ne, Hai Oppappi!" This translates to, "I Don't Give A Damn, Yes Oppappi!" The ringtone was first announced on a Japanese national T.V. program called _Music Station_ and had over 3,500 downloads that day. Cumulative sales of ringtone are over 20,000. Andrew's song debuted at No.1 in Label Mobile's International daily ringtone chart. Label Mobile is the biggest mobile retailer in Japan.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-99)

### Live music venue

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Live music venue")]

In the spring of 2008, Andrew and three partners opened a multi-level nightclub and live concert hall in downtown Manhattan, New York City. The venue was named [Santos Party House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Party_House "Santos Party House"), and featured 8,000 square feet (740 m 2) of dance floor and concert facilities, and over 150 loud-speakers.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-100) The space was designed for disco dancing and live music. It was one of the few new venues in New York City to be granted a liquor license and a cabaret license. The cabaret license means people can legally dance until 4 am.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-101) Santos Party House received numerous awards, including The People's Choice Award for Best Night Club, Best New Club, Best DJ Night (from _Paper Magazine_),[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-102) Best New Dance Floor (from _The Village Voice_),[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-103) and many more. In May 2009, Wilkes-Krier and his work with Santos was the subject of an extensive four-page article in _New York Magazine_.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-104) In 2010, the [Zagat Survey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zagat_Survey "Zagat Survey") rated Santos Party House the "Top Dance Club" in all of New York City.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-105)

Santos Party House's last night of operation was May 29, 2016.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-106)

## Legal disputes over name ownership

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Legal disputes over name ownership")]

In November 2004, W.K.'s official website was hacked with threats of blackmail from someone who claimed to have co-created Andrew W.K.'s persona, and demanded to be included in the production of the third album, claiming to be "Steev Mike".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-107) W.K. responded stating, "Please don't believe Steev Mike. I used to call myself Steev Mike a long time ago and it's nothing now. Someone is trying to confuse you and make me look bad."[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-used-108)

In subsequent years, W.K. denied various theories accusing him of being a fake entity, declaring himself to be "a real person who thinks for himself" and "not the victim of anyone or group of people trying to influence my career or life".[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-109)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-111) He clarified that "the nature of how we presented my initial offerings caused some confusion, even though I tried to make it as straightforward as possible... Different people I've worked with and different parts of my back story have gotten twisted and changed. But I made the music on my albums – I had a lot of help from incredible people, but not the kind of help that some people think."[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Front-112)

Due to legal disputes regarding the ownership of the name "Andrew W.K.", _[Close Calls with Brick Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close\_Calls\_with\_Brick\_Walls "Close Calls with Brick Walls")_ (2006) was initially only released in Japan and Korea. On August 18, 2007, it was given a limited release in America only on vinyl on [Load Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Load_Records "Load Records") with five exclusive bonus tracks, but only became widely available on CD to the rest of the world in March 2010, bundled with a second disc containing a collection of rare and unreleased songs entitled _Mother of Mankind_.

In September 2009, writing in the British newspaper, _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_, Andrew W.K. acknowledged legal disputes around his name: "At the end of 2004, an old friend of mine got in some business trouble and basically decided to take it out on me. To cut a long story short, this person is someone I worked very closely with and had a formal and family business relationship with. Due to various complaints this person had with me, they were able to turn my life and career upside down. I wasn't allowed to use my own name within certain areas of the US entertainment industry and we were in a debate about who owned the rights to my image, and who should get credit for 'inventing' it. This made my life complicated and intense for a few years, but I kept working and doing whatever I could to keep moving forward."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-33)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Andrew W.K. previously lived in [Midtown Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Manhattan "Midtown Manhattan") but left in 2006 or 2007, "bouncing between short-term situations" in other locations outside [New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state) "New York (state)").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-living-130)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Goodman-5) He married Cherie Lily on October 4, 2008, in a traditional Persian wedding ceremony.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-aboutwk-131) Lily performed with W.K.'s band as a vocalist and [hypewoman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hype_man "Hype man") from 2006 until 2018.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-132) W.K. has two children but keeps them out of the public eye.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-134)[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-135) W.K. has a younger brother, Patrick Wilkes-Krier, who is a professional golfer.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-136)

In May 2021, W.K. announced via a press release that he and his former wife Cherie had begun amicable divorce proceedings in late 2019. He also confirmed that he was dating actress [Kat Dennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kat_Dennings "Kat Dennings"), after the two met in Los Angeles in early 2021.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-137) A week later, on May 13, 2021, the couple announced their engagement on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-138) They married on November 27, 2023, at their Los Angeles home.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-139)

**Andrew Fetterly Wilkes-Krier** (born May 9, 1979), known professionally as **Andrew W.K.**, is an American singer, multi-instrumentalist, songwriter, record producer and motivational speaker. He is known for his combination of [rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_music "Rock music"), [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") and [pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pop_music "Pop music") music and anthemic songs about partying.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-4)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) Raised in Michigan, Wilkes-Krier began his musical career in the mid-1990s. He performed in a number of local bands before eventually moving to New York, where he produced his first recordings under the Andrew W.K. moniker.

After gaining initial attention with the 2000 [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play")_Girls Own Juice_, Wilkes-Krier rose to prominence with the release of his debut studio album _[I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Get\_Wet "I Get Wet")_ in November 2001, which was followed by _[The Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")_ (2003) and _[Close Calls With Brick Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close\_Calls\_With\_Brick\_Walls "Close Calls With Brick Walls")_ (2006). Legal troubles preventing Wilkes-Krier from releasing music in the US led up to him making the album _[55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55\_Cadillac "55 Cadillac")_ (2009), which consists of solo [improvisational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_improvisation "Musical improvisation") piano pieces.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Goodman-5) He returned to rock music with the albums _[You're Not Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Not\_Alone\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")_ (2018) and _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_ (2021). The instrumental [jazz-noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_jazz "Crime jazz") album _[Temptation to Exist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temptation\_to\_Exist?action=edit&redlink=1 "Temptation to Exist (page does not exist)")_ (2026) was [surprise released](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surprise_album "Surprise album") after a five-year hiatus.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-6) He has also undertaken a number of other musical and non-musical ventures including television and radio work, motivational speaking and writing.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Andrew Fetterly Wilkes-Krier[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-7) was born in [Stanford, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford,_California "Stanford, California"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) on May 9, 1979[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-livewire-9) and raised in the outskirts of [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), until moving to [Ann Arbor, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Arbor,_Michigan "Ann Arbor, Michigan") at the age of four.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-livewire-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-10) His father is professor [James E. Krier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_E._Krier "James E. Krier"), a legal scholar at the [University of Michigan Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_Law_School "University of Michigan Law School") and co-author of the widely used Dukeminier & Krier property casebook.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11) His mother is Wendy Wilkes. His younger brother, Patrick, was a golf professional and is now a golf coach in Michigan.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-12) At the age of four, Wilkes-Krier began learning piano at the [University of Michigan School of Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Michigan_School_of_Music,_Theatre_&_Dance "University of Michigan School of Music, Theatre & Dance").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Enders-13) He has recalled early family trips to [midnight mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_mass "Midnight mass") as having had an enormous impact on his love for music.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-14)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He was dubbed Andrew W.K. by an elementary school teacher to differentiate him from his classmates [Andrew Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Hawthorne "Mayer Hawthorne") and Andrew Gilchrist.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He later attended the private college preparatory [Greenhills School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greenhills_School "Greenhills School") for middle school before attending the alternative [Community High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_High_School_(Ann_Arbor,_Michigan) "Community High School (Ann Arbor, Michigan)") from 1993 to 1997, where he continued to study piano and keyboard.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Enders-13)

## Music career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Music career")]

### 1993–1999: Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1993–1999: Early career")]

In 1993, at the age of 14, he joined the band Slam, later to be called Reverse Polarity.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) In 1996, a song recorded by W.K. entitled "Mr. Surprise" was included on _Plant the Flower Seeds_, a compilation by the [Ypsilanti, Michigan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ypsilanti,_Michigan "Ypsilanti, Michigan")-based record label Westside Audio Laboratories, marking his first publicly released recording.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201418-17) Over the next five years, W.K. would play in a number of Detroit-based [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") and [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") bands,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) including The Pterodactyls; Lab Lobotomy; Music Band; Mr. Velocity Hopkins; playing drums in [grindcore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grindcore "Grindcore") metal band, Kathode;[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) in addition to forming the [noise rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noise_rock "Noise rock") project Ancient Art of Boar, later known as AAB, which served as an outlet for his early solo material.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)

In 1998, W.K. moved from Michigan to New York City, where he worked a variety of short-lived jobs. These included a bubblegum machine salesman, an opera ticket salesman, a fashion photographer, a window decorator at the [Bergdorf Goodman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bergdorf_Goodman "Bergdorf Goodman") department store, and a waiter for a Mexican restaurant. He also worked at the offices of the avant-garde fashion company [Comme des Garçons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comme_des_Gar%C3%A7ons "Comme des Garçons").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8) He ended the AAB project and began recording new solo material under his full "Andrew Wilkes-Krier" name; the year saw the release of a cassette-only single entitled _Room to Breathe_ on [Hanson Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanson_Records "Hanson Records").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) A follow-up release entitled _You Are What You Eat_ was scrapped when the master recordings went missing.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-18) W.K. also recorded the soundtrack for an independent film named _Poltergeist_ made by [Aaron Dilloway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Dilloway "Aaron Dilloway") and himself, one track of which appeared on the Hanson Records compilation _Labyrinths & Jokes_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) In 1999, he moved to [Seffner, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seffner,_Florida "Seffner, Florida"), to start building his live band with drummer [Donald "D.T." Tardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Tardy "Donald Tardy"), of [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal") band [Obituary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obituary_(band) "Obituary (band)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-popmusic-15)

### 2000–2003: Solo breakthrough, _I Get Wet_ and _The Wolf_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2000–2003: Solo breakthrough, I Get Wet and The Wolf")]

Main articles: [I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Get_Wet "I Get Wet") and [The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wolf_(Andrew_W.K._album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")

In March 2000, Wilkes-Krier released his first [EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), _Girls Own Juice_, also abbreviated as _AWKGOJ_, on [Bulb Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulb_Records "Bulb Records"), his first solo release under the moniker Andrew W.K. (He had first been credited as "Andrew W.K." on a remix entitled "Wolf Eyes Rules (What Kinda Band?)" for the experimental noise band [Wolf Eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf_Eyes "Wolf Eyes").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201452-19)) _Girls Own Juice_ introduced his [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock")-influenced musical style and experimental tendencies, described as "[Judas Priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judas_Priest "Judas Priest") mixed with [Sparks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparks_(band) "Sparks (band)")" by Magas, a collaborator of W.K.'s.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201453-20)

_Girls Own Juice_ was well received by critics, and was awarded a five-star rating by the British music magazine _[Kerrang!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerrang! "Kerrang!")._[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-21) The release increased buzz for W.K., centered around his "hedonistic, so-dumb-it's-smart rawk."[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) He continued to build his reputation by performing various solo gigs in the New York and other East Coast areas. Wilkes-Krier and his then manager [Matt Sweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Sweeney "Matt Sweeney") later shipped out a number of Andrew W.K. demo tapes, each accompanied by a handwritten letter. One tape reached [alternative rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternative_rock "Alternative rock") musician [Dave Grohl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Grohl "Dave Grohl"); impressed, Grohl offered Andrew W.K. a slot opening for his band [Foo Fighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foo_Fighters "Foo Fighters") at a concert in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), which he accepted.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22)

Another tape reached [The Island Def Jam Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Island_Def_Jam_Music_Group "The Island Def Jam Music Group") executive Lewis Largent, who liked the demos enough to attend an Andrew W.K. gig at the [Mercury Lounge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Lounge "Mercury Lounge"), where Largent was impressed by how W.K. "won over every last person in the audience."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22) Wilkes-Krier reacted with surprise to Island's interest in him, and despite his manager urging him not to accept his very first offer, W.K. was eager to begin work with Island.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-FOOTNOTECrandall201455-22)_Girls Own Juice_ was followed by another Bulb Records EP entitled _[Party Til You Puke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party\_Til\_You\_Puke "Party Til You Puke")_ in October 2000.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16) Following the release of _Party Til You Puke_, Andrew W.K. left Bulb Records amicably to sign with [Island Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Island_Records "Island Records").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-early-16)

W.K.'s major-label debut studio album, _[I Get Wet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Get\_Wet "I Get Wet")_, was released on November 13, 2001, on Island Records.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Klosterman-24) Continuing the sound established by his previous Bulb Records EPs, _I Get Wet_ is characterized by its [metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") and [punk rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock") influences and lyrical content revolving around partying.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) The album is known for its cover art, a photograph by [Roe Ethridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roe_Ethridge "Roe Ethridge") of Andrew W.K. with a stream of blood running from his nose onto his chin and neck,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-25) which generated minor controversy in Europe after it was seen to represent [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine") abuse;[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-26) W.K. claims to have achieved the effect by striking himself in the face with a cinderblock during the photo shoot, and subsequently supplementing his own blood with some of an animal obtained from a butcher's shop.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8)

_I Get Wet_ earned positive press from publications such as _[NME](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NME "NME")_ and _[Kerrang!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerrang! "Kerrang!")_ and featured two UK hit singles, "[Party Hard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Party_Hard_(Andrew_W.K._song) "Party Hard (Andrew W.K. song)")" and "[She Is Beautiful](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/She_Is_Beautiful "She Is Beautiful")", also rising to the top spot on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_'s [Top Heatseekers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Top_Heatseekers "Top Heatseekers") albums chart.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-27) She Is Beautiful was also featured on the 2003 [_Freaky Friday_ soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freaky_Friday_(soundtrack) "Freaky Friday (soundtrack)"). At the same time, W.K. also developed a reputation for his highly energetic live shows.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Bio-1) Andrew W.K. joined [Ozzy Osbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzy_Osbourne "Ozzy Osbourne")'s [Ozzfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzfest "Ozzfest") that summer, and a number of _I Get Wet_'s tracks, such as "Party Hard", "It's Time to Party", and "Fun Night" were licensed for use in various video games, films, TV series, and commercials. In 2002, W.K., Gibson Goodness and Alec Rominger re-recorded his song "We Want Fun" from _AWKGOJ_ for the soundtrack of _[Jackass: The Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackass:\_The\_Movie "Jackass: The Movie")_; an accompanying music video was also produced, filmed and directed by [Jeff Tremaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Tremaine "Jeff Tremaine") with additional camera work by [Spike Jonze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Jonze "Spike Jonze"). By September 2018, the album had sold 267,000 copies in the US.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-28)

In late 2003, W.K. released his second studio album _[The Wolf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wolf\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "The Wolf (Andrew W.K. album)")_. In contrast to _I Get Wet_, which was recorded by W.K. with his live band, _The Wolf_ featured W.K. playing all instruments, with heavy use of [overdubbing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overdub "Overdub") of these instrument sections in production. The album spawned the singles "Tear It Up" and "Never Let Down" in the United States, while the song "Long Live the Party" was a minor hit in Japan. The single "Tear It Up" was included as menu music in the video-game Nascar Thunder TM 2004.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11) Despite earning Andrew W.K.'s highest chart position ever at #61 on the Billboard 200, it fell off after only a week,[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-29) and three months after its release the album had only sold 36,098 copies.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-30)

On tour for _The Wolf_, W.K. was injured on stage and broke his foot. After the concert, he signed autographs from the ambulance. Not wanting to let his fans down, he performed the remainder of the tour in a wheelchair.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-loudwire-8)

### 2004–2008: _Close Calls with Brick Walls_

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2004–2008: Close Calls with Brick Walls")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4e/Andrew_WK.jpg/250px-Andrew_WK.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Andrew_WK.jpg)

W.K. in 2006

Main article: [Close Calls with Brick Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close_Calls_with_Brick_Walls "Close Calls with Brick Walls")

Though _[Close Calls with Brick Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Close\_Calls\_with\_Brick\_Walls "Close Calls with Brick Walls")_ failed to see wide release in 2006, W.K. continued to be active; he released a live concert DVD entitled _[Who Knows?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Knows%3F\_(album) "Who Knows? (album)")_ in February of that year and presenting five screenings of the film in New York and Hollywood.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-page5-31) In March 2006, during an episode of [Sex Pistols](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Pistols "Sex Pistols") guitarist [Steve Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Jones_(musician) "Steve Jones (musician)")' radio show _Jonesy's Jukebox_, W.K. debuted a new song entitled "I'm a Vagabond".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-page5-31) On November 26, 2008, under [Universal Music Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Music_Group "Universal Music Group"), he released his fourth studio album, _[The Japan Covers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Japan\_Covers "The Japan Covers")_, which consists of cover versions of [J-pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J-pop "J-pop") songs, as well as a compilation entitled _The Very Best So Far_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-page5-31)

### 2009–2019: _55 Cadillac_, _You're Not Alone_ and other releases

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2009–2019: 55 Cadillac, You're Not Alone and other releases")]

Main articles: [55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55_Cadillac "55 Cadillac") and [You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're_Not_Alone_(Andrew_W.K._album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")

In February 2009, Wilkes-Krier claimed to have found a loophole in his contractual constraints allowing him to form his own record label, Skyscraper Music Maker, based in London and Manhattan.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-label-32) The label released _DAMN! The Mix tape Vol. 1_ on May 25, 2009, a compilation of W.K.'s production work for Skyscraper Music Maker artists Bad Brilliance, Aleister X, and [Cherie Lily](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherie_Lily "Cherie Lily"), with music by New York producer, DJ B-Roc.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-label-32) Wilkes-Krier's fifth studio album _[55 Cadillac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55\_Cadillac "55 Cadillac")_ served as the label's second release. Recorded entirely by Wilkes-Krier and consisting of his spontaneous solo piano improvisations, the album was released on September 8, 2009.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-33) In a piece written to accompany the release of the album, he explained that the last decade had "been so fraught with legal trouble" that he began to suffer hallucinations, which inspired him to produce the album, and that successful negotiations had allowed him to start a new label and release _55 Cadillac_, which he described as "the sound of a piano being played by a free man – nothing more, nothing less."[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-guardian.co.uk-33) New negotiations were undertaken over the UK release of _55 Cadillac_, as "certain people [who] weren't credited because they weren't involved with the recording... had to be given credit," owing to previous contracts.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) Wilkes-Krier and his management settled by renaming Skyscraper Music Maker as Steev Mike, which the parties involved saw as a reasonable compromise.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) All prior complaints were dropped and Wilkes-Krier was then allowed to release the album worldwide.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34)

On September 9, Andrew W.K. released a Japan-only album entitled _[Gundam Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gundam\_Rock "Gundam Rock")_, consisting of covered music from the [Gundam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gundam "Gundam") anime television series to celebrate its 30th anniversary in Japan; he had been approached by Japanese animation studio [Sunrise Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunrise_(company) "Sunrise (company)") to record the album following the success of _The Japan Covers_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-37) With all prior legal disputes over credit and naming settled, in March 2010 Andrew W.K. and the newly named Steev Mike label presented its first official release: a repackaged two-disc version of _Close Calls with Brick Walls_ with a bonus disc of rare and unreleased material entitled _Mother of Mankind_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Rocksound-34) To promote the set, Andrew W.K. joined the 2010 [Warped Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warped_Tour "Warped Tour") as a headlining act for the entire tour.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Warped_Tour_2010-38) A music video for the single "I Want to See You Go Wild" from _Close Calls with Brick Walls_, directed by [Peter Glantz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Glantz "Peter Glantz"), was released in June 2010.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-39)

In March 2011, Andrew W.K. released a new EP entitled _[The "Party All Goddamn Night" EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_%22Party\_All\_Goddamn\_Night%22\_EP "The \"Party All Goddamn Night\" EP")_, which consists of five new tracks and two previously released singles.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-40) In September 2012, while attending a fan convention for _[My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Little\_Pony:\_Friendship\_Is\_Magic "My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic")_, he expressed the possibility of recording a new album.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-41) In a [Reddit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reddit "Reddit") "Ask Me Anything" thread in October 2014, Wilkes-Krier stated that while his other career ventures had kept him from releasing a new studio album, he was eager to record one: "I've been stock-piling new songs for several years. I really want to make a new album as soon as possible."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-42)

In September 2017, W.K. announced that a new studio album would be set for release on March 2, 2018, via [Sony Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-43) In November, he announced its title, _[You're Not Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You're\_Not\_Alone\_(Andrew\_W.K.\_album) "You're Not Alone (Andrew W.K. album)")_, and shared its cover artwork.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-45) The album was released on March 2, 2018. In August 2018 he revealed to _Riff Magazine_ that he had begun recording his next album.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-46)

### 2020–present: Napalm Records, _God Is Partying_, _Temptation To Exist_ and current ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2020–present: Napalm Records, God Is Partying, Temptation To Exist and current ventures")]

Main article: [God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God_Is_Partying "God Is Partying")

In October 2020, Andrew W.K. signed with [Napalm Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Napalm_Records "Napalm Records") and announced that he was working on a new album.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-47) The lead single "Babalon" was released on February 17, 2021.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-48) "Babalon" was announced via a Napalm Records press release and made available for limited pre-order on the Napalm Records and Andrew W.K. stores as a 7" vinyl with the instrumental B-Side "The Party Gods".[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-:0-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-50) The release, limited to 393 copies, marked a departure from Andrew W.K.'s traditionally positive and uplifting themes, and features "swinging drums and a sinister guitar riff opening the track's hellish gates."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-:0-49)

Andrew W.K.'s sixth studio album, _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_, was released on September 10, 2021.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-51) Co-produced by long-time recording partner Ted Young, the nine-track album features W.K. performing all instruments.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-52) The announcement was accompanied by the release of a new single, "I'm in Heaven".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-53) On July 14, 2021, the video for "Everybody Sins" was released and features an appearance by [Kat Dennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kat_Dennings "Kat Dennings").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-54) In September 2021, the album _[God Is Partying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/God\_Is\_Partying "God Is Partying")_ was released alongside the single "Stay True To Your Heart".[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-56)

Shortly after the release of the album, W.K. delayed upcoming shows and deleted his website and social media pages with no explanation; his label also remained quiet on what was happening.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-58)

On August 28, 2026, W.K. released the album _Temptation to Exist_ on the fan run website AWKSHARE and through YouTube Music. [[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-59)

## Other ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Other ventures")]

### Self-help and motivational performance

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Andrew_W.K.&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Self-help and motivational performance")]

During 2007, Andrew performed a series of unpredictable [happenings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Happening "Happening") as part of his "One Man Show" tour. Each event began with Andrew improvising on the piano alone on a stage before they frequently evolved into giant parties, with most of the audience dancing on stage with Andrew, themselves playing the piano and singing the lyrics.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)

In March 2007, _[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_York\_Times "The New York Times")_ put Andrew on the front page of its Arts section, in a feature article on Andrew's lectures.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-60) In 2008, Andrew's self-help work led to his second appearance as a sit-down guest on _[Late Night with Conan O'Brien](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Late\_Night\_with\_Conan\_O'Brien "Late Night with Conan O'Brien")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-61) In November 2008, _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(magazine) "Time (magazine)")_ magazine called him "truly cute".[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-bio-11)

In June 2012, W.K. announced that he would be appearing at the _[My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Little\_Pony:\_Friendship\_Is\_Magic "My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic")_ fan convention Canterlot Gardens.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-62) His appearance was announced as a motivational seminar on "How to Party like Pinkie Pie", based on one of the show's lead characters, Pinkie Pie. The appearance was featured in _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-rollingstone.com-63) and was co-hosted by musician and personality Klisk Midori.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-Klisk-64)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-rollingstone.com2-65)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-everfree.net-66)

In June 2014, Andrew was announced to speak as a guest lecturer at the [Oxford Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_Union "Oxford Union").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-67) W.K.'s keynote, titled _Andrew W.K. and The Philosophy of Partying_, discussed his signature message of positive power and celebratory self-confidence. Regarding the lecture, Oxford's Nick Fowler said: "In my opinion, Andrew is one of Rock N' Roll's great philosophers." And the Oxford University Rock Society offered their own statement: "We've seen rock stars, we've seen brilliant public speakers, but rarely are they the same person, and rarely do they have as intriguing and broad a background as Andrew W.K."[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-68)

In September 2014, Andrew gave a lecture on his philosophy of partying at [Baltimore School for the Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baltimore_School_for_the_Arts "Baltimore School for the Arts") as part of The Contemporary museum's speaker series called "CoHosts".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-69) In the same month, he also brought his Village Voice advice column, "Ask Andrew W.K.", to life in an intimate setting at New York City nightclub, [Santos Party House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Party_House "Santos Party House").[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-70)

In February 2018, Andrew was named the Person of the Year by the [American Association of Suicidology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Association_of_Suicidology "American Association of Suicidology").[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-71) The AAS stated, "The inaugural Person of the Year Award will be presented to Andrew W.K. due to his consistent and powerful use of positivity to improve the lives of those who hear his music."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_W.K.#cite_note-72)
